motion: Does consciousness fundamentally pervade reality and point toward God?

moves.currentDescription: Biology and the wider cosmos exhibit directionality toward complexity, diversity, value, and purpose that is not merely invented by humans.
moves.lockedProposition: Biology and the wider cosmos exhibit directionality toward complexity, diversity, value, and purpose that is not merely invented by humans.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I think science has tried in the past and has finally given up um trying to say there is no directionality or purpose. And um I I think physics accepted it, but biology has been dragging its feet. So, you get ridiculous things like you mustn't say a turtle comes ashore to lay her eggs. It It'll comes ashore and lays her eggs, as though these things were unconnected. But I think there is directionality in biology very obviously. And there is also in the cosmos at large. And if I look back to what we know of the cosmos before we were here to um to to know very much about it, the two things seem to be um a sort of growth in complexity. And I would say a growth into diversity, a sort of beautiful multiplicity. So, out of one came many, but the many didn't threaten the integrity of the one. It's like the unfolding of a bud into a flower doesn't ruin the bud. It is the fulfillment of the bud. And I That's the way I see the development of things in the cosmos. And much to my surprise, in the book the matter of things, when I come to the last part, which is ontology or metaphysics or whatever you like to call it, I knew I was certainly going to talk about matter and consciousness and space and time and things like that. But I didn't know that I was going to have separate chapters on value and purpose. But it seemed to me that these are particularly crucial. In the last 15 years, my thinking has been very much more about what these things are doing there. And that they are not simply made up by us.

moves.sectionTitle: Teleology and the inference to God
moves.currentDescription: Open-ended teleology points not to a divine engineer but to an infinitely creative relational ground from which things emerge.
moves.lockedProposition: Open-ended teleology points not to a divine engineer but to an infinitely creative relational ground from which things emerge.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: But I need to qualify what I mean there, because I don't think there is a fixed purpose. I absolutely resist the idea of a tinkering god, an engineering god. This is an expression of the left hemisphere's desire to have everything under control and sorted out and a little bit more um 3-in-One oil and the thing will be beautifully. I don't believe this is whatever I mean by god. Whatever I mean is a a ground of infinite creative potential that is looking for the existence of relation. I think every I mean, I argue in that book and this is all not again probably where you want the conversation to be, but I argue that relations are primary. They are prior to things, prior to relata.
